notes: Each run operates on a fresh clone of the fixture at scratchpad/fixtures/android-catalog-fixture — a real Android app (AGP + Kotlin, Compose BOM, git-initialized on `main`) with an intentionally outdated version catalog. Report highlights: gson 2.10->2.14 [safe] and androidx core-ktx 1.13->1.19 [safe minor]; a Compose BOM 2024.06.00 whose CHILDREN (compose-ui, material3) show updates but are BOM-governed and must be IGNORED (bump only the BOM); AGP 8.7.3 -> 9.2.1 [MAJOR, coupled with the Gradle wrapper -> defer]; kotlin 2.0.21 + ksp [coupled block]; a swarm of AGP-governed com.android.tools.utp:* tooling artifacts that are noise and must be ignored; and a catalog-only JitPack lib com.github.barteksc:AndroidPdfViewer [the plugin's blind spot]. Verify with `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug`. The <FIXTURE> token is replaced with the per-run copy path. Prompts pre-authorize the safe subset so the gated flow can proceed to apply/verify/commit without a human at the gate.

evals.prompt: I've got an Android project at <FIXTURE> that uses a version catalog (gradle/libs.versions.toml). Check what dependencies are outdated, show me a proposal grouped by risk, then go ahead and apply just the SAFE (low-risk, same-major) updates and commit them locally — you have my confirmation for the safe subset. Leave anything risky like a major bump for me to decide.
evals.expected_output: Runs dependencyUpdates, presents a risk-grouped proposal that (a) proposes bumping only the Compose BOM and explicitly ignores the BOM-governed compose-ui/material3 children, (b) classifies AGP 8.7.3->9.2.1 as a MAJOR coupled with the Gradle wrapper and defers it, (c) ignores the AGP-governed com.android.tools.utp:* tooling noise, and (d) flags the JitPack lib for manual review. Applies the safe subset (gson, core-ktx, compose BOM) to libs.versions.toml, verifies with ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug, commits on a non-default branch with a chore(deps) message, and responds in English.
assertions: Detected available updates by running the gradle-versions-plugin (dependencyUpdates) or reading its report, rather than inventing versions.
Recognized that compose-ui and material3 are governed by the Compose BOM and proposed bumping only the BOM (did NOT propose the child artifacts as separate items).
Classified AGP 8.7.3 -> 9.2.1 as a MAJOR (coupled with the Gradle wrapper) and did NOT apply it.
Identified the JitPack library com.github.barteksc:AndroidPdfViewer from the catalog as a manual-review item (did not silently miss it).
Did not propose the AGP-governed com.android.tools.utp:* tooling artifacts as catalog updates (recognized them as noise).
Presented a proposal BEFORE editing any file (gate respected).
Applied only safe updates to gradle/libs.versions.toml (e.g. gson and/or core-ktx and/or the compose BOM; no AGP major).
Ran ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug (or a build) to verify after editing, and it succeeded.
Committed on a NON-default branch (not main) with a chore(deps) style message and did not push.
User-facing response is written in English.

assertions: Explicitly located the JitPack entry com.github.barteksc:AndroidPdfViewer by reading the catalog, noting the gradle-versions-plugin does not track it.
Attempted to determine its latest stable version via JitPack metadata (maven-metadata.xml) or GitHub releases.

Applied only safe updates to gradle/libs.versions.toml.
Ran ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug (or a build) to verify after editing, and it succeeded.
Committed on a NON-default branch with a chore(deps) style message.
User-facing response is written in English.
